record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: Do there exist left-symmetric algebras that produce the algebras or operators arising in the F-type singularity construction, and equivalently is there an intersection between this class of singularities and scalar-type singularities?

evidence.quote: (3) Are there any left-symmetric algebras that produce such algebras/operators? In other words, is there an intersection of this class of singularities and scalar type singularities.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $L : TM \to TM$ a Nijenhuis operator, i.e., a $(1,1)$-tensor field whose Nijenhuis torsion
\[
\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y) := L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]
\]
vanishes identically. A point $p \in M$ is called a singular point of scalar type if $L(p) = \lambda \cdot \mathrm{Id}$ for some $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. At such a point, the tangent space $T_pM$ inherits a canonical structure of a left-symmetric algebra (LSA, or pre-Lie / Vinberg–Koszul algebra), that is, a bilinear product $\ast$ on a vector space $A$ satisfying
\[
(x \ast y) \ast z - x \ast (y \ast z) \;=\; (y \ast x) \ast z - y \ast (x \ast z) \qquad \text{for all } x,y,z \in A,
\]
obtained by linearizing $L$ at $p$.

A separate class of singular points of Nijenhuis operators, called F-type singularities, is defined by a different normal-form / linearization procedure that produces a specific associated algebra (or operator) at the singular point.

Problem. Do there exist left-symmetric algebras whose associated linearized Nijenhuis operator realizes the algebras (or operators) arising from the F-type singularity construction? Equivalently, is the class of F-type singularities of Nijenhuis operators intersected non-trivially by the class of scalar-type singularities, and if so, characterize all such common singularities.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on Nijenhuis geometry (including a 2025 preprint on the linearization of certain singularities of Nijenhuis operators) continue to investigate scalar-type singularities via left-symmetric algebras and F-type singularities as distinct constructions, but no source found resolves the question of whether the two classes intersect or identifies LSAs producing F-type operators. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Linearization of Certain Singularities of Nijenhuis Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies linearization of Nijenhuis operator singularities, including scalar-type and F-type singularities, without resolving their intersection.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research treats scalar-type and F-type singularities separately; no characterization of their overlap is given.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry II: Left-symmetric algebras and linearization problem
status_evidence.snippet: Left-symmetric algebras correspond to linearizations of Nijenhuis operators at scalar-type singular points.
status_evidence.claim: LSAs classify scalar-type singularities, providing the framework in which the question is posed.
